engagement_title: Meridian and Ash sticker range and counter programme: recover the painted window mark and three printed bag illustrations into real cut artwork, gang them onto the printer's sheet with a separable cut layer, rebuild last season's shelf card into a live six origin run, and hand back the on sale set editable
vertical: Food and beverage, specialty coffee roasting and retail, one roastery cafe plus two market stalls and roughly forty wholesale accounts (Portland, Oregon)
real_brief_anchor: The ledger row for VECTOR-04 carries an empty real_brief_anchors array, so the anchor is the recurring posted commission this concept was carved from rather than a single quoted post. The shape recurs constantly on Upwork and Freelancer.com under titles of the form 'die cut sticker sheet design for our coffee brand' and 'convert my logo to vector for stickers', and the body is always the same three asks: turn our existing logo and artwork into vector, arrange the designs on one print ready sheet, and supply the cut lines, with 'vector files' and 'editable source files' named among the deliverables and the client volunteering that all they have is a photograph or a printed sample because the original designer is gone. The ledger's own one_line_ask is quoted verbatim into the client voice here: pull our logo and a few of our existing printed illustrations into clean sticker art, and lay it all out as a die-cut sheet plus individual stickers we can sell and hand out. The triage verdict on the row is STRENGTHEN, and the reason it needed strengthening is that as carved it sat almost entirely on one surface (trace, then lay out), which is not the commission a roastery of this size actually places. Two things change that. First, the ledger's own 'peel-mockup card' would be photo compositing, which is not connector work, so it is re-carved as the printed counter card the roastery already puts in front of each origin, and that card is a genuine record per page run off a press PDF they already own. Second, CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) makes authored fixed canvas layout at true sheet size real, with inline SVG arriving as native editable vector, so the sheet and the on sale set are one editable document rather than a flat picture. That is the fuller job this client genuinely places inside one month.
client_one_liner: Our sign painter put the mark on the shop window eight years ago and we never got a file, our illustrations only exist printed on bags, and our sticker supplier redraws all of it slightly differently every batch.
client_brief:
Meridian and Ash, sticker range and counter programme

We roast in a converted machine shop in Portland and sell across our own counter, at two farmers markets and to about forty wholesale accounts. Stickers are half our merchandise table. We buy them in from a supplier who redraws our artwork every time, and every batch comes back a little different from the last one. People notice.

We want our own range. Six designs: the mark from our shop window, the three illustrations that are already printed on our bags, and two more that we work out with you and that have to look like they belong with the others. Three dollars for a single, nine dollars for a four pack, and we hand them out by the fistful with wholesale orders, so there will be a lot of them and the range should feel like there are a lot of them.

What we can give you. A photograph of the shop window, because the painter never gave us a file. Photographs of the bags, because the illustrations only exist printed on bags. And our printer still has the artwork for the shelf card that sits in front of each origin at the counter, from last season.

What we need back. Each sticker as artwork with nothing behind it that we can print at any size, so nobody ever redraws them again. All of them arranged on one sheet the way a sticker printer wants them. The cut line has to come as its own thing the printer can lift off, because our last supplier baked it into the picture and the press operator ended up redrawing it by hand.

We also need the counter cards for our six current origins, one card per origin, printed the same way as last season so they sit in the same holders. And a small on sale set: one square, one tall, one wide, in one file we can change ourselves, because the designs will rotate.

Playful, generous, a bit hand made. Not precious, not boutique. Our customers are twenty to thirty five and these go on laptops and water bottles.
price_band_and_audience: Impulse retail at three dollars a single and nine dollars a four pack, buyer twenty to thirty five, a cafe regular who buys at the till without deciding first. The band is load-bearing. At this price the range has to read as abundant and hand made: many small pieces, a warm printed ground, generous ink coverage, type that looks painted rather than set. The same six marks treated as a luxury programme, one foil emblem on a deep matte ground with acres of air, misreads the till entirely: it prices like a forty dollar object, it kills the four pack, and it makes the giveaway handful look like a mistake. Push the other way into loud discount styling, heavy outlines, drop shadows and a crowded sheet, and it stops reading as a roastery that people want to advertise on a laptop lid. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even when every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 700 to 1,800 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Specialty coffee roaster and cafe selling stickers and merchandise at the till, at farmers markets and to wholesale accounts.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2016, Portland, Oregon, a converted machine shop with one counter, two market stalls and roughly forty wholesale accounts.
brand_identity.about: Meridian and Ash roast single origin coffee in a converted machine shop and sell it across their own counter, at two farmers markets and to about forty wholesale accounts. The merchandise table is half the fun: stickers people put on laptops and water bottles because they actually like the mark. The whole point is a range that feels made by hand, not bought by the case.
brand_identity.audience: Cafe regulars twenty to thirty five who buy a sticker at the till without deciding first, and wholesale buyers who hand them out with orders.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Impulse retail, three dollars a single and nine dollars a four pack. Priced to be handed out by the fistful, so the range has to read as abundant rather than precious.
brand_identity.typography: A shaded serif wordmark that looks painted rather than set, arched over a filled roundel. Text and labels lean into a friendly, slightly irregular hand. Nothing boutique or foil thin.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, warm, a little wry, never precious. Example line: Pull one off the sheet, stick it on your laptop, come back for the other three.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No usable source files exist. The window mark was hand painted on the shop glass in 2018 by a sign painter who never handed over a file. The three current illustrations survive only printed on the coffee bags, and the printer still holds last season's counter card artwork.
brand_identity.values: Consistency people can trust, so the artwork stops being redrawn slightly differently every batch, and a hand made feel that reads as a real roastery rather than a franchise.

assets_supplied.name: meridian_window_mark.jpg (4160 x 3120)
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the shop window from the sidewalk, the mark hand painted in two inks on the glass: a shaded serif wordmark arched over a filled roundel that carries an ash leaf inside a hairline ring.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only place the mark exists. Ross painted it in 2018 and we never got a file off him."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a compound lockup painted on glass, which behaves nothing like a flat scan. A prompt naming the window or the glass returns the pane rather than the paint, a compound prompt returns the arched wordmark while silently dropping the ring and the leaf and still looks entirely plausible, and the one call knockout cannot punch the ring's enclosed interior so it returns a solid opaque disc. Across the right third the street reflects in the glass at close to the value of the darker ink.

assets_supplied.name: meridian_bag_illustrations/ (3 frames, 5472 x 3648)
assets_supplied.kind: Flat lay photographs of three printed coffee bags, one illustration on each: a moth, a ridge line, a pour over cone.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The three that are already on the bags. We want those exactly as they are, they are the reason people pick us up."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the three were printed as solid ink and the third was screened at press. At photograph preview scale a screen reads as a flat tone and is indistinguishable from solid ink, so nothing about the frame declares which is which. It only announces itself once the ink is traced, as thousands of dot contours instead of a drawing. Separately one of the three crosses the bag's gusset fold, so part of its geometry is bent off the plane and does not straighten with the frame.

assets_supplied.name: meridian_shelfcard_2025.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's press artwork for last season's counter card, one card per origin, the file that actually went to press.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our printer sends this back every season. The holders on the counter are cut for it, so the card cannot change size."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The card's origin name, roast line, tasting notes and price were set as one continuous flow, so what the converted document exposes as separately addressable frames is nothing like the four blocks the printed card shows. And the readout of the card's own story omits one run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed and every offset past it is short by that run's length, while the mapping validates clean and the prepare call reports success.

assets_supplied.name: meridian_origins.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Plain data for the six current origins: origin, farm, process, roast, tasting notes, price.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The six we are pouring now. The notes are what our head roaster wrote, do not improve them."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the six carry a second tasting line the other four do not, so those two rows are roughly twice the length of their neighbours, and one row's price is the wholesale per pound figure rather than the counter price, which no column header distinguishes and no cell flags.

assets_supplied.name: meridian_sheet_spec.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The sticker printer's note: sheet size, minimum gutter between cuts, safe margin from the sheet edge, and their standing requirement that the cut contour arrive as its own separable object rather than drawn into the artwork.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What our printer sent when we asked what they need."

acceptance_bar: Every sticker is placeable scalable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath it, and nothing behind it on any ground.

Each sticker still reads as the same drawing at the size it actually reproduces, on the printed ground it actually sits on, not only at full canvas. A mark whose interior closes at fifty five millimetres fails even though it looks correct enlarged.

The cut contour is one closed offset path per sticker at the offset the printer's note states, held as its own separable object in the delivered layout, not a halo drawn into the picture and not the artwork's own edges.

The six designs read as one range: one ink language, one weight of line, one amount of hand. A recovered mark that arrives crisper or fuzzier than its neighbours is named rather than shipped alongside them.

The gang sheet is at the printer's true sheet size in real physical units, with the stated gutter and safe margin honoured, and the arrangement is justified against vinyl yield and counter readability rather than eyeballed.
Six counter cards, one origin per page, page count equal to row count, every field on every card carrying this season's copy and none still carrying last season's.
Every counter card is the same trim as last season's card so it sits in the existing holders, and the card that is delivered is press artwork, not a screen scale proxy.

All three on sale canvases sit in ONE working file, each keeping its own canvas size, with live text we can retype and the mark as real vector shapes, delivered alongside the self contained source it was built from.
No delivered file exceeds the pixel dimensions of the frame it came from, and no resize any tool performed goes unreported.

A written note stating what was recovered from where, which design could not be recovered as drawn and what was done instead, the type by role with family and actual weight, and anything the printer needs to know about the cut layer.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_invert_selection, image_crop_to_bounds, image_fill_area, image_apply_adjustments (masked), image_remove_background (transparent and backgroundColor routes), image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs and detection_confidence), image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: All four recoveries and the printed ground. It takes the painted mark off glass at ink level rather than pulling the pane, decides per illustration between the two colour trace off the binary mask and the colour accurate knockout plate, produces the transparent raster proofs the printer's RIP preview wants, and performs the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not do for you: injecting a viewBox and removing the opaque full canvas path that otherwise rides along onto the sheet.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The gang sheet at the printer's true sheet size and the three on sale canvases, in one native editable document. This is the only surface in the connector that composes free form fixed canvas layout. Each sticker and each cut contour goes in as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, the printed ground is inlined as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, and the payload travels by uploaded URL because inlined photography passes the inline threshold immediately.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (as generator and as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout, document_render_layout
adobe_surfaces.role: The six counter cards, rebuilt from the press artwork the roastery already owns so the cards still fit the holders on the counter. This is the only route to a genuine record per page run at volume, and the only honest way to justify a field map is to export the interchange file and read what the conversion actually exposes before promising one.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: One type system carrying the sheet, the on sale canvases and the two new designs. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land on hand made and abundant rather than boutique. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, every name has to be laundered into canonical form before the kit call because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS has to use the returned slug or it falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the printed ground the roastery does not own, a kraft board surface at genuine camera scale with generative tech candidates excluded, which is then selected as a material by prompt, warmed and cropped to a repeating tile. The Boards half persists the range selects the two owners sign off from, placed within the twelve per call cap, with a partial success read as partial and vector understood to be unboardable.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: The stickers and the ground are raster and vector work, the sheet and the on sale set have to be an authored fixed canvas document because the client will rotate designs themselves, and the counter cards are a record per page run because the holders fix the trim. The brief pins all three destinations, so there is nothing to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming the surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handover discipline: a manifest keyed by role so that thirty artefacts later the agent still knows which URL is which bag.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Look at the window photograph and all three bag frames, and triage them: where paint and reflection run close in value, what each mark is actually made of, which frame is off level, which illustration crosses a fold.
trajectory.judgement: The client believes there are four recoveries of the same kind. The pictures are the only thing that can settle whether that is true, and looking at a thumbnail is not the same as looking at the frame.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering substrate, ink behaviour, tilt and where ground and mark run close.

trajectory.action: Straighten the bag frames that sit off level, before any bounds decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Recover the window mark: an ink level selection worded from the paint's own visual properties rather than from the surface it sits on, the correct polarity, a bounds crop driven by the selection's own returned box, then a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions no tool makes: how to word the selection so it takes the paint and not the pane, which polarity to trace, and whether the two colour trace or the colour accurate knockout plate is the deliverable. A one call knockout on an enclosed ring is the wrong instrument entirely.
trajectory.produces: A placeable transparent mark plus a colour accurate variant, with the recovery route recorded.

trajectory.action: Recover the three bag illustrations the same way, one frame at a time, choosing per illustration between the two colour trace off the binary mask and the colour accurate knockout plate, and inspect each traced result rather than the response.
trajectory.judgement: They came off three different bags and they are not three of the same job. What each one is made of decides which route is correct, and the response text says the same thing either way.
trajectory.produces: Three traced illustrations with their route and their path behaviour recorded per frame.

trajectory.action: Draw the two new designs as authored inline SVG geometry, built from the stroke weight, terminal and corner language the recovered marks actually have.
trajectory.judgement: They have to look like they came off the same hand. That is a construction decision taken from the recovered artwork, not a style chosen freely, and at this band it has to stay generous rather than becoming precise.
trajectory.produces: Two new sticker designs as editable vector geometry consistent with the recovered four.

trajectory.action: Derive the cut contour for each of the six as a single closed offset path at the printer's stated offset, held as its own object, and decide what happens where a design has enclosed interior negative space.
trajectory.judgement: A die cut is not the artwork's own edges. The offset direction, the treatment of interior holes and the decision to simplify a contour the blade cannot follow are all craft calls the printer will otherwise make with a pen.
trajectory.produces: Six closed cut contours, each separable from the artwork it belongs to.

trajectory.action: Search short generic queries for a kraft board surface, filter to photography, exclude generative tech candidates, license and download at full resolution, then select the paper surface by prompt, warm it and crop it to a repeating tile.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the house warmth rather than the prettiest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera scale frame and a printed ground tile derived from it.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's, judged against a three dollar impulse buy and a twenty to thirty five year old buyer. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author the gang sheet at the printer's true sheet size in absolute physical units, all six stickers and all six cut contours as inline SVG in explicitly sized top left anchored wrappers, gutters and safe margin taken from the printer's note. Lay two arrangements, a tight pack and themed rows, and pick one.
trajectory.judgement: The pick is argued on vinyl yield and on whether a customer can read the range at arm's length in a counter bin. An auto sized or right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the sheet edge, so everything is anchored and sized.
trajectory.produces: A sheet layout at true physical size with a stated arrangement rationale.

trajectory.action: Author the three on sale canvases as three further roots at their own canvas sizes in the same document, the ground tile inlined as image data, the mark as inline SVG, family and weight declared on every text element.
trajectory.judgement: A global canvas override is exactly what collapses a mixed size set, so each root declares its own. The design work is how much air an abundant range can carry before it starts pricing like a boutique.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the sheet and the on sale set, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, upload the HTML and export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first artboard, and parse the returned per canvas markup for everything else.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning of any kind, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at one page is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first artboard, and a per canvas markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's shelf card artwork, export the interchange file, and read what the conversion actually exposes as addressable frames and what the card's story text actually says, before promising any field map.
trajectory.judgement: What a press PDF exposes is a property of how it was set, not of how it looks printed. Promising a per field map before looking is promising something nobody has checked.
trajectory.produces: A frame inventory and the card's own story text, read from the interchange file.

trajectory.action: Build the mapping, prepare the merge template, then merge the six origins one record per page and render at press resolution at the card's existing trim, and look at what came back.
trajectory.judgement: The holders fix the trim, so the card cannot be resized to solve a copy problem. The two long tasting rows and the row carrying a wholesale figure are content decisions the merge will not make.
trajectory.produces: A six page press file at the existing trim plus per record files, with the merged pages actually inspected.

trajectory.action: Create the range selects board, add the transparent proofs and the licensed frame within the per call placement cap, re-sending only the entries the response names as failed, then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success, and vector is not boardable so it belongs in the note instead. The note has to be specific enough that the next freelancer does not repeat the archaeology.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which of the three bag illustrations was screened at press rather than printed in solid ink. At the scale a photograph of a bag previews at, a press screen reads as a flat tone and is visually identical to solid ink, so nothing in the frame, the filename or the client's description separates them. It declares itself only in the traced result: the two solid marks come back as a drawing with a countable number of contours, and the screened one comes back as thousands of dot contours that still assemble into a plausible looking picture at full canvas and only fall apart as artwork at sticker size and as an editable object once placed.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it, because the tracing tool takes no options at all and the only lever is what the raster prep hands it, which is the decision this checkpoint is about. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the three illustrations are already printed on the bags and that the client wants them exactly as they are. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the affected illustration goes through a different chain, a binary ink mask traced as a mask rather than a colour plate traced as art, or a redraw as authored geometry when the screen has destroyed the line.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-derive that one illustration through a different route, judge whether what comes back is still the drawing on the bag or a new drawing wearing its shape, and then re-place it, which changes its silhouette and therefore its cut contour and its position in the sheet arrangement.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A range where one of six stickers is a cloud of dots that prints muddy at fifty five millimetres and arrives in the client's editable file as thousands of loose shapes, on a merchandise line whose entire premise is that nobody ever has to redraw the artwork again.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: That the readout of the shelf card's own text is short of the truth. The card's copy was set as one continuous flow, so the conversion exposes nothing like the four blocks the printed card shows, and the readout of that flow omits one run while keeping its line break, leaving a string that still looks well formed. Every offset computed past the omission is short by that run's length. The validator returns valid with no warnings on those offsets, the prepare call reports completing successfully, and the only place the shortfall appears is on the merged page, where two fields still carry last season's copy while the rest carry this season's.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the readout is the only description of the story the tools volunteer, and there is no flag, warning or count that says a run is missing. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the printer still has last season's artwork and that the cards must stay the same size. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is to reconstruct the card's true story text out of the interchange file and recompute every offset against that string, which is a different derivation, not the same derivation repeated.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the field map from the reconstructed story text, prepare the template again, confirm by round tripping the interchange file that every placeholder is actually present rather than trusting the success message, then re-merge and read the six pages.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Six counter cards that look right and print right and quietly tell every customer at the till the wrong tasting notes and the wrong price for two of the six origins, with every tool response in the chain having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the thing the whole deliverable turns on. The printer needs the cut contour as a separable object sitting over the artwork, and the natural authoring constructions for it are exactly the ones this importer discards without saying so: an outline is dropped entirely, a stroked display letterform loses its stroke and can render as fully transparent, a blurred halo is dropped so the element goes hard edged, and a stacked shadow is truncated to its first layer. All of them return success. The returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports it, and the document's own rendition returns the first artboard only, so whichever canvas is not first cannot be checked any other way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step, and doing it right the first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks only that the cut line arrive as its own thing the printer can lift off. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a different construction of the same object, a closed path drawn as real geometry with its own fill and stroke rather than a CSS effect around the artwork, and the sheet then has to be re-composed around what that object actually is.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the cut layer as authored path geometry, re-author the sheet and the on sale canvases around it, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit every canvas from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A gang sheet delivered as an editable file with no cut layer in it at all on the canvases nobody looked at, sent to the printer who then does exactly what the last supplier's press operator did and redraws the cut by hand, which is the specific thing the client hired this job to stop.

deliverables.name: Meridian and Ash sticker artwork masters
deliverables.spec: Six sticker designs as placeable scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: four recovered from photographs of painted and printed originals and two authored to match their construction. A real viewBox present on each, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, one ink language and one weight of line across the six, and each still reading as its own drawing at the size it actually reproduces.

deliverables.name: Cut layer, one closed contour per sticker
deliverables.spec: Six single closed offset paths at the offset the printer's note states, each held as its own separable object rather than drawn into the artwork, with interior negative space resolved deliberately and any contour simplified for the blade named as simplified. Delivered as real path geometry that survives into the editable document, not as an effect applied around a picture.

deliverables.name: Gang sheet at the printer's sheet size
deliverables.spec: One sheet at the printer's true sheet size in real physical units, all six designs ganged with the stated minimum gutter and safe margin honoured, the arrangement chosen between a tight pack and themed rows and justified on vinyl yield and counter readability, with the cut layer present and separable on the sheet.

deliverables.name: Transparent sticker proofs
deliverables.spec: Six transparent raster proofs at press scale for the printer's preview, carrying genuine alpha rather than a white rectangle, each cut from its own source frame with the cut edge holding under close inspection rather than at preview scale, and none exceeding the pixel dimensions of the frame it came from.

deliverables.name: Six origin counter cards
deliverables.spec: One card per current origin at the same trim as last season's card so the existing counter holders still fit, page count equal to row count, every field carrying this season's copy, plus per record files for the printer whose identity is guaranteed per call rather than by position in a returned list. Rendered at press resolution rather than at screen scale.

deliverables.name: On sale set and handover
deliverables.spec: One native editable document carrying three roots at three canvas sizes with live editable text in one licensed type system and the mark as real vector shapes, delivered with the self contained source it was authored from, paired with a written note recording what was recovered from where, which design could not be recovered as drawn and what was done instead, the type by role with family and actual numeric weight, every resize any tool reported, and what the printer needs to know about the cut layer, alongside a persistent shareable selects board.

verifiers_auto.text: Every delivered sticker SVG has a viewBox attribute and no full canvas opaque background path at path index zero.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse each delivered SVG: assert a viewBox is present and assert the first path's geometry does not span the whole canvas.

verifiers_auto.text: Each sticker has exactly one closed cut contour associated with it, and that contour exists as its own object rather than as a stroke or effect on the artwork element.
verifiers_auto.how: Count closed subpaths per cut object and assert each cut object is a sibling of, not an attribute on, the artwork it belongs to, in both the source HTML and the returned per canvas markup.

verifiers_auto.text: The sheet root declares the printer's stated sheet size in absolute physical units and the export returned it at the corresponding pixel size.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the root's declared canvas size in the source and the per slide width and height in the export response, and convert against the printer's note.

verifiers_auto.text: The export returned four roots, each keeping its own declared canvas size, and no global canvas override was passed.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are recovery work, which need an authored fixed canvas document, and which need a record per page run, given that only one surface here composes free form layout and only one produces volume personalisation.

Selection wording on the painted window: naming the window or the glass takes the pane, naming the paint's own visual properties takes the mark, and a one call knockout on an enclosed ring is the wrong instrument entirely.
Which recovery route each of the four originals needs, since a two colour trace off a binary mask and a colour accurate knockout plate produce different artwork and the response text is identical.
Whether a recovered illustration is still the drawing on the bag or has become a new drawing wearing its shape, and what to tell the client when it is the second.
How the two new designs are constructed, taken from the recovered marks' own stroke weight and terminals rather than chosen freely.
Cut contour craft: offset direction, what happens to enclosed interior negative space, and when to simplify a contour the blade cannot follow.
Tight pack versus themed rows on the sheet, argued on vinyl yield against readability in a counter bin.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a three dollar impulse buy, plus the real numeric weight per family.
Whether the licensed kraft frame joins the range's world or reads as bought, and how warm the ground can go before the ink stops separating from it.
What to do about the row carrying a wholesale figure and the two rows carrying a second tasting line, when the trim is fixed by the holders and cannot absorb them.
How much air the on sale canvases carry. At this band abundance is the design, and a spare, single emblem treatment is a correct looking wrong answer.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the photographs into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of coffee stickers. IDENTITY: this is the mark a sign painter put on this roastery's window in 2018 and three illustrations that are already printed on bags customers recognise on the shelf, and the entire reason the job exists is that a supplier keeps redrawing them slightly differently. A regenerated mark is precisely the failure the client is paying to stop. SPEC: the printer needs six closed cut contours at a stated offset as separable objects on a sheet at a real physical size with a stated gutter, and the counter cards must land at last season's exact trim so the existing holders still fit, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the sheet and the on sale set are defined by being editable, because the six designs rotate and the owners cannot re-commission each time. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: is this illustration solid ink or a press screen, does this cut layer still exist after the import, did two of the six cards quietly keep last season's copy.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, fill_area, apply_adjustments masked, remove_background in both forms, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs, auto_straighten and vectorize are verified headless across 27 live calls, and the extract and reuse chain ending in a native editable Express document was run end to end. The recovery checkpoint rests on documented findings rather than assumptions: vectorize TAKES NO OPTIONS AT ALL, so a binary mask in gives two colours out and a colour plate in gives dozens of near identical fills out, and a traced mark arrives in Express as many loose ungrouped shapes. The substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry, the compound mark partial selection, the solid disc failure of remove_background on an enclosed ring, the missing viewBox and the opaque path zero are all live findings, and the acceptance bar scores exactly the hygiene the tool does not perform. EXPRESS: multiple roots at mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, absolute physical units resolve exactly at 96 dpi, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, clip path polygon becomes a real path, and the product is a genuine editable document findable by asset_search. The import checkpoint rests on verified drops: outline dropped entirely, filter blur dropped, multi layer shadow truncated to layer one, text stroke dropped leaving fully transparent text, all at HTTP success with no warning, and the rendition preview documented as first artboard only. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the 70 KB threshold immediately, and every photo is base64 inlined because a URL renders as an empty grey box. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt as generator and validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout and document_render_layout are all verified headless and synchronous, one record per page for PDF is verified with page count equal to row count, and the mapping checkpoint rests on the verified lossy readout that dropped a 17 character run while keeping its line break, shifted every later offset, validated clean and landed only 3 of 5 mappings. Per record identity is taken through the verified createSeparateFiles or recordRange routes rather than by position, because multi record raster URLs came back reversed. Press resolution is taken through document_render_layout because merge output silently ignores resolution. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, a real full resolution licensed JPEG, and boards persisting with a cap of 12 placements per call and 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no photo compositing anywhere including the re-carved counter card, no upscaling, no OCR, no text to image, no generative fill, no variable QR, no bleed claim off a PDF derived template, no pdfPreset, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above 20.
